app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:199 — ensure_embeddable's only gate is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; the Referer header is fully attacker-controlled for any non-browser HTTP client (curl, script), so this "check" provides no real access control and is trivially bypassed to obtain the ALLOWALL framing response and trigger retrieval for any embed_url.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:201 — response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` disables clickjacking protection for this controller's responses; combined with the spoofable referer check above, effectively any page (or non-browser client crafting the header) can have this content framed with no real host restriction enforced.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:182 — params.require(:embed_url)` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` on a public, cross-origin, iframe-rendered endpoint with no explicit rescue/friendly response defined in this diff; the spec at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:798 expects "not be_success" but doesn't pin the exact status, so third-party callers that mistakenly omit `embed_url` (or embed.js failing to base64/urlencode correctly) get an undocumented generic error response rendered inside their page rather than a stable, versioned error contract (e.g. a proper embed-branded error view/status).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` does call `params.require(:embed_url)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` if `embed_url` is absent. However, that’s standard Rails behavior for required parameters and typically results in a 400 Bad Request (often via Rails’ built-in handling), not an introduced correctness/security bug by itself. Additionally, the controller is guarded by `before_filter :ensure_embeddable`, so many “public” calls without the right referer/host won’t even reach the `params.require` line. The proposed finding is mainly about UX/API contract expectations (a branded error view / pinned status), which is not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:4 — New `cook_method` column defaults to `1`, which is only correct if `Post.cook_methods` (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)) is 1-indexed with :regular==1; if the Enum is zero-indexed instead, every existing/new post would default to :raw_html and Post#cook would return unrendered raw content instead of cooked HTML (could not verify Enum indexing in this checkout)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `cook_method` is an integer column with `default: 1` and that `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. However, whether `1` corresponds to `:regular` or `:raw_html` depends on how `Enum` assigns values, and `Enum`’s implementation is not part of this diff. The finding is explicitly conditional (“if the Enum is zero-indexed”) and cannot be verified from the provided changes alone. Additionally, this codebase already uses the same `Enum.new(...)` pattern for `Post.types` (pre-existing), strongly suggesting the indexing scheme is already established and consistent, making the concern speculative in the context of this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — create_table :top_topics, force: true` drops and recreates a pre-existing table, destroying any existing top_topics data on migration re-run/deploy

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an old migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` does drop/recreate the table if it already exists, Rails does not re-run already-applied migrations on deploy, so this change will not affect existing installations that have already run this migration. For fresh databases, the table won’t exist yet, so nothing is “destroyed”. The finding’s claim about data loss on “migration re-run/deploy” is therefore not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff in normal operation (it’s only relevant in atypical scenarios like manually re-running this exact `up` with an existing table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` on `create_table :topic_embeds` is superfluous/misleading since the table is new (empty prior migration file), but signals a risky copy-paste pattern that caused the top_topics data-loss bug

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` that uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. While `force: true` can drop an existing table if it already exists, in the normal Rails migration flow this migration runs once on a database where `topic_embeds` does not yet exist, so it does not introduce a concrete, verifiable bug by itself. The proposed finding is largely a style/risk-nit (“superfluous/misleading”) and the claim about signaling/copy-paste causing other data-loss is speculative and not a direct defect shown in this file/diff context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` in `import_remote` has no read/open timeout, so a slow/hanging remote host can block the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely (invoked from both the on-demand RetrieveTopic job and PollFeed)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using `open-uri` without specifying any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, it does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and this is called from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is used by the on-demand `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` flow. A slow/unresponsive remote host can therefore tie up a Sidekiq worker thread for an unbounded/very long time (at least until underlying defaults/OS-level timeouts/DNS resolution return), since no explicit timeouts are set in the code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` for the RSS/Atom fetch has no timeout, so a hung feed server stalls the hourly scheduled job with `retry: false`, silently skipping that run

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, and it does not pass explicit timeouts. However, the finding’s claim that this has “no timeout” and can “hang indefinitely” is not verifiable from the diff alone because Ruby’s `open-uri`/`Net::HTTP` have default open/read timeouts depending on Ruby version/config (not shown here). Also, if the request did hang, the Sidekiq worker would remain blocked rather than “silently skipping that run”; with `retry: false` it won’t retry on exceptions, but a hang isn’t an exception/skip. So the finding overstates behavior that isn’t clearly established by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — perform_retrieve` synchronously calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (a full feed fetch+parse) inline inside the on-demand `RetrieveTopic` regular job triggered per web request; an unresponsive/hanging feed URL blocks per-request embed jobs, not just the hourly scheduled job, and any exception raised there propagates and aborts `fetch_http` too

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` contains:

```rb
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end

fetch_http
```

`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (new in this diff) does a synchronous `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `SimpleRSS.parse(...)` and then iterates items. There is no timeout handling or rescue in either `TopicRetriever` or `PollFeed`, so a slow/hung feed URL will block the `RetrieveTopic` worker that invoked `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, and any exception during feed fetching/parsing will bubble up and prevent `fetch_http` from running. This behavior is directly verifiable from the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` result/failure is not checked; if enqueuing raises (e.g. Redis/Sidekiq unavailable) the request errors instead of degrading gracefully, and the client only finds out via the 30s auto-reload in the loading view

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and then immediately `render 'loading'`. There is no explicit error handling around the enqueue, so if `Jobs.enqueue` were to raise an exception the request would indeed error. However, the finding’s stated impact is not accurate: if enqueue raises, the controller would not render the loading view, so the client would see an error response immediately (not “only find out via the 30s auto-reload”). Also, “not checking the enqueue result” is not a clear defect by itself—job enqueues typically return an ID and failures are handled via exceptions, so the absence of a result check is not verifiably a bug introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:150 — TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` in the batch import task has no rescue, so one bad/slow remote link aborts the entire disqus import run instead of skipping that thread

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import loop now does `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` with no surrounding `begin/rescue`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document.new(...)` without any error handling; network errors, invalid URLs, HTTP failures, or parsing exceptions will raise and bubble up, terminating the Thor task mid-run. This is a verifiable robustness/correctness regression versus the prior code path that didn’t fetch remote content per-thread.
